labels.label: T-abs-ladder-local-defs/locally-push-up
labels.notes: LocallyPushUp (∀ x, ∃ W : Opens M, x ∈ W ∧ C.PushUpOn W) is the inline hypothesis (hcover, hO) of CausallyArcConnected.pushUp (ArcConnected.lean:343-344, ι : Type v, O : ι → Opens M) up to the existential over the cover: an auditor probe proves LocallyPushUp ↔ ∃ (ι : Type u) (O : ι → Opens M), cover ∧ ∀ i, PushUpOn (O i), and locallyPushUp_of_cover takes ι : Sort*, so every universe of the original is covered. CausallyArcConnected.pushUp_of_locallyPushUp is choose + the original, no hypothesis added. Paper sentence (lem:pushup_local, ETT.tex:557-559) quoted verbatim in the docstring. PushUp.locallyPushUp, locallyPushUp_iff_nhds, PushUpOn.mono, dual_locallyPushUp proved.

labels.label: T-abs-ladder-local-defs/locally-causally-open
labels.notes: LocallyCausallyOpen := LocallyCausallyOpenFuture ∧ C.dual.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture is (hloc, hloc') of AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpen (Minimal.lean:124-126): `Iff.rfl` probe passes. Restated witness = original applied to hloc.1 hloc.2. locallyCausallyOpen_iff (one neighbourhood for both sides) proved; CausallyOpen.locallyCausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpen.future, dual lemma proved. Two-sidedness is the DEC-8 ruling, not a closer reading.

labels.label: T-abs-ladder-local-defs/chronal-neighbours
labels.notes: ChronalNeighbours := ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours is (hZm, hZp) of causallyOpen_of_pushUp (LemmaK.lean:93-98) definitionally (`Iff.rfl` probe against the two inline ∀ V, ∀ v ∈ V, ∃ p ∈ V, … forms passes), and matches the ladder `under` (ladder.toml, edge push_up ⇒ causally_open). The re-proof PushUp.causallyOpen_of_chronalNeighbours has exactly the strength of the LemmaK statement (probe: it yields CausallyOpen from PushUp, hZm, hZp) and is the same proof; LemmaK is model-importing (its closure reaches Causal.Minkowski, Causal.Static, Causal.Model.*, Causal.Flat.*), so the re-proof is what the dispatch asked. Separation lightlikeLine_separates_chronalNeighbours states PushUp ∧ CausallyOpen ∧ GloballyHyperbolic ∧ NoCausalEndpoint ∧ ¬ ChronalNeighbours, as reported. AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalPastNeighbours_iff [T1Space M] states what the finding says. Past as base direction is disclosed (question), compatible with kb/0002 (which fixes no base). See finding 1 on the wording of the second REPORT finding.

labels.label: T-abs-ladder-local-defs/no-causal-endpoint
labels.notes: NoCausalEndpoint := NoPastEndpoint ∧ C.dual.NoPastEndpoint is (hpast, hfut) of inextensibleNestedOn_top / GloballyHyperbolic.inextensibleNestedOn_top (NestedCausalities.lean:433-436, 450-452) and (hJm, hJp) of ChainsCurves.lean:366-367 definitionally (`Iff.rfl` probe against ∀ x, C.Jminus ⊤ {x} ≠ {x} ∧ ∀ x, C.Jplus ⊤ {x} ≠ {x} passes); the paper's J^±(p) ≠ {p} (theo:geroch, ETT.tex:1258-1259, quoted verbatim) read as both signs. Both restated witnesses pass the original's arguments in order (no added hypothesis). ChainsCurves and LemmaK witnesses not restated: they import Causal.Minkowski / models (checked), disclosed in SCOPE and REPORT. Separation spacelikeLine_separates_noCausalEndpoint states PushUp ∧ CausallyOpen ∧ GloballyHyperbolic ∧ ¬ NoCausalEndpoint, as reported; its non-tarentin caveat is disclosed and correct (≪ empty, singletons have empty interior).

labels.label: T-abs-ladder-local-defs/one-sided-boundary
labels.notes: OneSidedBoundary (dom i₁) (closure S) is honesided of ers_theorem_4_82 (NestedCausalities.lean:1405-1406) verbatim (`Iff.rfl` probe passes); ers_theorem_4_82_of_oneSidedBoundary passes every argument of the original in order. Non-vacuity: oneSidedBoundary_Ioi_zero and not_oneSidedBoundary_compl_zero. The docstring's claim that ERS (4.83) gives OneSidedAt at each p ∈ ∂U₁ ∖ ∂S is mathematically correct (shrink the box: base ball B with f(B) ⊂ (f(x₀)−η, f(x₀)+η); the part below the graph has non-empty interval fibres, hence is connected), and is disclosed as unformalised (layer 3); it makes the Lean hypothesis weaker, so Lean ≥ (4.83). The ∂S finding is correct: S ⊆ U₁ open misses frontier U₁, so frontier U₁ ∖ closure S = frontier U₁ ∖ (closure S ∖ S); under any reading with ∂S ⊆ closure S the Lean hypothesis is implied by ERS's. ERS text (eperon2018predictability.txt:2029-2033) quoted faithfully. No causality argument: disclosed as a question for the keeper.

findings.what: "So the converse of push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours ⇒ causally_open fails, and the side condition of that edge is genuine" does not follow from the cited witness if 'genuine' is read as 'needed': the lightlike line is itself causally open, so it shows only that chronal neighbours are not a consequence of push-up (and of causal openness, GH, no causal endpoint), not that push-up alone fails to give causal openness. The stronger statement is true, but by another example: the auditor checked in Lean (probe under /tmp, deleted; standard axioms) a causality on ℝ with ≪ = ∅ and ≤_U the diagonal plus the single pair 0 ≤ 1 (0, 1 ∈ U), which has push-up (vacuously) while J^+_ℝ((−1,1)) = (−1,1] is not open.
